props.gloss_en: R' Akiva: I once went into the privy after R' Yehoshua and learned three things from him
one does not relieve oneself facing east and west, but north and south
one does not uncover oneself standing, but sitting
one does not wipe with the right hand, but with the left
Ben Azzai to R' Akiva: were you so impertinent to your teacher?
R' Akiva: it is Torah, and I must learn
Ben Azzai: I once went into the privy after R' Akiva and learned three things from him
R' Yehuda to Ben Azzai: were you so impertinent to your teacher?
Ben Azzai: it is Torah, and I must learn
Rav Kahana: Abba's mouth is like one who has never tasted a cooked dish
Rav: Kahana, you are here? leave, for it is not proper conduct
Rav Kahana: it is Torah, and I must learn
Rava: because the Torah was given with the right hand
as it is said: 'from His right hand, a fiery law unto them' (Deut 33:2)
Rabba bar bar Chana: because it is near the mouth
Reish Lakish: because one ties tefillin with it
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: because one points out the taamei Torah with it
the stam: [the amoraim's disagreement] is like [a disagreement of] tannaim
R' Eliezer: because one eats with it
R' Yehoshua: because one writes with it
R' Akiva: because one points out the taamei Torah with it
R' Tanchum bar Chanilai: whoever is modest in the privy is saved from snakes
...and from scorpions
...and from demons
some say: even his dreams are settled for him
a privy in Tiberias harmed those who entered two together, even by day; R' Ami and R' Asi entered it each alone and were not harmed
the Rabbis to R' Ami and R' Asi: are you not afraid?
R' Ami and R' Asi: we have learned a tradition -- the tradition for the privy is modesty and silence
...the tradition for suffering is silence and prayer for mercy
Abaye's mother raised a lamb to go into the privy with him
before Rava was head [of the academy], Rav Chisda's daughter would rattle a nut in a copper vessel for him
after he was appointed, she made him a window and placed her hand on his head
Ulla: behind a fence, one relieves oneself at once
Ulla: in a valley, far enough that if he breaks wind his fellow does not hear
Isi bar Natan teaches: behind a fence, far enough that if he breaks wind his fellow does not hear
Isi bar Natan: in a valley, far enough that his fellow does not see him
the mishnah: those who go out of the olive press's entrance and relieve themselves behind the fence are pure
the mishnah: how far may they go and remain pure? so far that he [still] sees him
Rav Ashi: Isi bar Natan's 'so long as his fellow does not see' means does not see his nakedness; the man himself he may see
the eulogizer: this man was modest in his ways
Rav Nachman to the eulogizer: did you go into the privy with him, that you know whether he was modest or not?
the baraita: one is called modest only if modest in the privy
the baraita: as punishment is exacted from the dead, so it is exacted from the eulogizers and from those who answer after them
the stam: Rav Nachman insisted because the eulogizers too are punished
the baraita: who is modest? one who relieves himself at night in the place where he relieves himself by day
Rav (via Rav Yehuda): a person should always accustom himself [to relieve himself] morning and evening, so that he will not need to distance himself
Rava by day would go as far as a mil, and at night told his attendant: clear me a place in the town street
R' Zeira told his attendant: see who is behind the study hall, for I need to relieve myself
the stam: do not read 'in the place', read 'in the manner in which he relieves himself by day'
Rav Ashi: even if you say 'in the place', it is needed only for a corner
Ben Azzai: rise early and go out, wait for evening and go out, so that you need not distance yourself
Ben Azzai: touch and then sit; do not sit and then touch
Ben Azzai: whoever sits and then touches -- even if sorcery is worked in Aspamia, it comes upon him

if he forgot and sat and then touched, his remedy: on standing he says 'not for me, not for me, neither tachim nor tachtim, neither these nor any of these, neither the sorceries of a sorcerer nor of a sorceress'
Ben Azzai: lie on any bed except the ground
Ben Azzai: sit on any seat except a beam
Shmuel: sleep at dawn is like tempering to iron
Shmuel: relieving oneself at dawn is like tempering to iron
Bar Kappara (who sold sayings for dinars): while you are hungry, eat; while you are thirsty, drink; while your pot is boiling, pour
Bar Kappara: when the horn sounds in Rome, son of a fig-seller, sell your father's figs
Abaye to the Rabbis: when you enter the paths of Mechoza to go out to the field, look neither to this side nor to that
Abaye: perhaps women are sitting there, and it is not proper conduct to look at them
Rav Safra was in the privy; R' Abba came and cleared his throat at the door; Rav Safra said to him: let the master enter
the mishnah: there was a fire there and a privy of honour, and this was its honour -- found locked, it was known someone was there; found open, it was known no one was there
R' Abba: so [speaking in the privy] is not proper conduct
the stam: and he [Rav Safra] held that he [R' Abba, holding back] was in danger
RSBG: a held-back mass brings a person to dropsy
RSBG: a held-back stream brings a person to jaundice
R' Elazar was in the privy; a Roman came and pushed him out; R' Elazar rose and left; a serpent came and tore out the Roman's gut
R' Elazar read of him: 'and I will give man [adam] in your stead' (Isa 43:4) -- do not read adam but Edom
